reason: The cited evidence discusses exchange bias and coercivity enhancement in FM/AFM systems (E2) and the role of disorder/uncompensated spins (E1, E3), but none of it involves CrFeCoNi alloys, Cr2O3 surface layers, or controlled oxidation treatments. The key premise that a Cr2O3 layer on this specific alloy will form a functional FM/AFM interface is unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Cr2O3 is antiferromagnetic and can form on CrFeCoNi alloy by controlled oxidation
A thin, uniform Cr2O3 layer creates a well-defined FM/AFM interface
Exchange coupling at FM/AFM interfaces increases coercivity via domain wall pinning
The coercivity enhancement persists below the blocking temperature of the AFM layer
Chemical disorder or uncompensated spins at the interface enhance exchange bias
